summary: 1937 enclosed timber lookout in the San Jacinto Wilderness, volunteer-staffed since 1998; the Forest Service and Mountains Foundation pages showed it closed when read.

facts.design: 20-ft enclosed timber tower with a 14 x 14 ft R5 wooden cab

access.note: When read, the Forest Service page showed a temporary-closure notice and a closed-for-the-season banner, and the Mountains Foundation said it was currently closed. Neither copy showed a date. The record listed the site as public; check before going.

visit.trail_note: 4.5-mile hike by the Devil's Slide or South Ridge trail; wilderness permits from the Idyllwild Ranger Station.

events.note: Original California Region 5 Plan 4A cabin built at a lower site, later moved to the summit and replaced by the current lookout
Working fire lookout until the end of the 1993 fire season
Restored in 1998 and returned to service in October
Reopened in October 1998 with volunteer staffing
October 2017 register visit: stairs need repair; rotten wood on the supports; paint peeling
Rotten wood replaced on Tahquitz Peak and Keller Peak, per the 2017 chapter report

notes_for_editor: District: the register (OCR 'ldyllwild') says Idyllwild Ranger District and the Forest Service page says San Jacinto Ranger District with an Idyllwild office; the story uses the Forest Service name and cites both. Closure status is the main open question: the Forest Service page (temporary-closure notice, closed-for-the-season banner, posted hours) and the Mountains Foundation (currently closed) are both undated copies, and the record says public. The access level is set to closed; re-check before publishing. Elevation disagrees across sources: register 8,752 ft (2,668 m; the record's 2,667.6 m comes from here), Mountains Foundation 8,828 ft, Forest Service 8,846 ft. The record is left unchanged. The 77-year figure is not explained by any source. It would be close to 77 years if counted from the 1917 cabin, but that is my inference only. The 2017 chapter report spells the peak Taquitz, and it says America Core kids (the record says youth crews); the story says young helpers. The register text has typos (ldyllwild, suppports) that I left out of quotes or copied as printed.
